description:
- Rewrite `if matches!(val, pat) { .. }` expressions as `if let pat = val { .. }`
- Replace `if matches!(..) {..}` with `match` expressions where it makes code easier to understand
- Use combinator methods instead of imperative code in a few places.
- Slay the [beast](https://github.com/nushell/nushell/compare/69857c108ca4070bc95e3618c8bd4a475a2ecf9d...c430bcde6f0f5941f9f2c8fff71ffdfe061ae073)

comments.body: I think that is one of the gray areas where the `matches!` form maybe has a benefit of making it more obvious what we care about first namely that we match the right hand side (and then you read all the covered patterns)

I have to admit I often forget that there are slice patterns ^^

I have to say that the previous code is hard to read, but i get the tendency of it of trying to write "top down procedural prose" that gets slightly hidden by more complex matches.

But I think your rewrite is easier on the eyes :)

```suggestion
        if input.empty() {
```

We should just call the `empty` method here. Clippy also has a warning for that if you try something similar. https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/stable/index.html#comparison_to_empty
